title: Tensor cohomology comparison from models of good truncations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with Grothendieck topology $J$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $B$ any commutative ring, and $R$ its constant commutative-ring sheaf, regarded as a ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Write $c$ for constant module presheaf sheafification along the ring unit [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $P,Q$ be K-flat cochain complexes of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Suppose $H^j(P)=0$ for $b_P<j$ and $H^j(Q)=0$ for $b_Q<j$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Fix an integer $i$ and an object $U$. Let $E,F$ be complexes of finite free $B$-modules, each zero in sufficiently high degrees. Suppose the standard derived category of $R|_U$-modules has isomorphisms
$$(\tau_{\ge i-b_Q}P)|_U\simeq c(E)|_U,\qquad (\tau_{\ge i-b_P}Q)|_U\simeq c(F)|_U.$$
Then, writing $T=\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_B F)$, there is an isomorphism of $R|_U$-module sheaves
$$H^i((\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q))|_U)\simeq H^i(c(T)|_U).$$
Here truncation is good lower truncation [def-kun-truncations], total tensor is the signed direct-sum total complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and restriction is to the slice site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No Noetherianity or local constancy hypothesis is imposed; the local models are supplied as data.

proof.text: Translate the acyclic-tensor hypothesis to the source K-flat predicate using the homotopy-category acyclic criterion and its braiding. The source bounded flat model theorem applied to good upper truncation gives flat representatives with the stated upper term bounds. The generic bounded-above flat criterion makes them K-flat. Tensoring the two quasi-isomorphisms and applying QObjTensorQObjIsoOfKFlatLeft gives the comparison with derived tensor. Functorial flat resolutions of module sheaves are supplied by hasFunctorialFlatResolution_kfi.

Prove that slice restriction preserves finite limits by sectionwise evaluation. Prove preservation of countable colimits by the slice sheafification comparison, lifting every sheaf diagram to presheaves by the sheafification counit. Use sliceTensorIso and its naturality for the tensor comparison. Flatness of restricted objects follows from the finite-limit component of restriction-flatness and the closed symmetric tensor structure.

For each factor, map the short exact good-truncation triangle through restriction and then through the appropriate left or right derived tensor functor. The source upper tensor bound puts the discarded tensor in degrees at most i-1. The long exact homology sequence makes the middle-to-right map an isomorphism in degree i. Identify the quotient term with good lower truncation. This applies also when a cutoff is above the upper bound.

The constant module presheaf of a flat B-module is tensor-flat by evaluation of limits. Sheafification preserves this flatness. Constant realization preserves countable colimits by evaluation and sheafification; its tensor isomorphism is the constant-presheaf tensor identity followed by the sheafification tensor comparison. Naturality assembles this into the signed total-complex comparison using mapBifunctorComparison.

Use the supplied local derived isomorphisms for both truncated factors. The first finite free constant model is bounded above and termwise flat, hence K-flat; the source K-flat tensor comparison therefore computes the tensor with the second model, with no flatness or upper bound of the second model required. Compose with the constant-realization and restriction total-tensor comparisons, then take degree-i homology and its factorization through Q.

theorem site_tensor_local_model_comparison
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (B : Type u) [CommRing B]
    (P Q : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (𝓡(J, B))) ℤ)
    (hP : P.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat) (hQ : Q.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat)
    (bP bQ : ℤ)
    (hPb : ∀ j : ℤ, bP < j → IsZero (P.homology j))
    (hQb : ∀ j : ℤ, bQ < j → IsZero (Q.homology j))
    (i : ℤ) (U : C) :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (SheafOfModules.{u} ((𝓡(J, B)).over U))
    ∀ (E F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ)
    (hEb : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, b < j → IsZero (E.X j))
    (hFb : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, b < j → IsZero (F.X j))
    (hE : ∀ j : ℤ, Module.Free B (E.X j) ∧ Module.Finite B (E.X j))
    (hF : ∀ j : ℤ, Module.Free B (F.X j) ∧ Module.Finite B (F.X j))
    (eE : Nonempty
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
            (P.truncGE (i - bQ))) ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          ((((cB(J, B)) ⋙ overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj E)))
    (eF : Nonempty
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
            (Q.truncGE (i - bP))) ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          ((((cB(J, B)) ⋙ overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj F))),
    let T := CochainComplex.mapBifunctor E F (MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor (ModuleCat B))
    Nonempty
      ((((overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
          (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor P Q
            (@MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor _ _ (monoidalCategory
              ((constantSheaf J CommRingCat.{u}).obj (CommRingCat.of B)))))).homology i ≅
        ((((cB(J, B)) ⋙ overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex
          (.up ℤ)).obj T).homology i)
